name: NGINX
summary: An event-driven network server that uses a master and worker process topology, nonblocking connection processing, configuration-built module graphs, and bounded memory ownership for request data.

features.name: Master-worker process topology
features.description: NGINX separates configuration and process supervision in a master process from request and connection handling in worker processes, with configuration and resources represented in a cycle inherited by workers.
benefits: Allows workers to handle connections concurrently without sharing all process state
Supports graceful reload and worker lifecycle control
costs: Process coordination and resource inheritance must be handled explicitly
Shared state requires dedicated shared-memory or synchronization mechanisms

features.name: Event-driven connection processing
features.description: NGINX workers process socket readiness through an event core and platform-specific notification modules such as epoll, kqueue, and select, rather than dedicating a blocking thread to each connection.
benefits: Handles many concurrent connections with bounded worker resources
Uses platform-specific readiness mechanisms behind a common event boundary
costs: Handlers must preserve nonblocking progress and correctly resume partial operations
A blocking operation in a worker can affect unrelated connections

features.name: Configuration-built module graph
features.description: NGINX builds a runtime cycle from configuration, module arrays, listening objects, paths, open files, and shared-memory zones; HTTP, stream, mail, core, and event functionality are organized as modules.
benefits: Makes deployment behavior configurable without changing request-processing code
Provides extension boundaries for protocol and event functionality
costs: Configuration validity and module ordering affect runtime behavior
Reloads must preserve or deliberately replace resources across cycles

features.name: Pool and buffer request lifetime
features.description: NGINX uses pools for scoped allocation and buffers/chains for input and output data, tying cleanup and reuse to connection, request, or cycle lifetimes.
benefits: Reduces per-object allocation bookkeeping for common request paths
Makes cleanup handlers and buffer ownership explicit at scope boundaries
costs: Pool lifetime errors can retain more memory than an individual object needs
Buffer chains require careful handling of partial consumption and reuse

mathematical_views.question: How do readiness notifications, partial I/O, timers, and protocol handlers advance a connection?
assumptions: A connection can move between readable, writable, waiting, and closing states
Handlers return control to the event loop when progress requires more I/O
The model abstracts operating-system notification details behind event modules

mathematical_views.question: Which state is private to workers and which state is inherited or shared across NGINX processes?
assumptions: Worker-local connections and pools are process-local
Configured shared-memory zones represent explicit cross-process state
The master-worker relationship is modeled as lifecycle coordination, not arbitrary shared memory

mathematical_views.question: How does configuration select the modules, listeners, resources, and protocol phases active in a runtime cycle?
assumptions: Configuration parsing produces a cycle with typed module and resource entries
Module hooks define phase participation and resource setup
The graph describes composition and ordering constraints rather than proving configuration correctness

benefits: Process isolation and controlled reload behavior
costs: Cross-process state and lifecycle coordination add operational complexity

benefits: High connection concurrency with a small number of workers
costs: Nonblocking handlers and partial-progress state are harder to implement
Configuration and module interactions expand the deployment state space

benefits: Fast scoped allocation and explicit buffer reuse
costs: Scope mistakes can cause retention or use-after-lifetime defects
